question: Why did two decades-long studies of calorie-restricted monkeys reach opposite conclusions about lifespan?
answer: Their control monkeys ate differently. At Wisconsin the controls ate freely from a diet high in sugar, so restricted animals looked healthier and lived longer. At the US National Institute on Aging the controls got measured portions of a more natural diet and were already fairly lean. The restricted monkeys there did not outlive them.
move: Every effect is measured against a baseline; ask what the baseline was doing.
ask: What baseline was a result measured against, and what was it doing?
reference: Mattison, Colman, Beasley et al., Caloric restriction improves health and survival of rhesus monkeys, Nature Communications, 2017
